q: What happens if a recursive function has no reachable base case?
options: It recurses until the call stack overflows (RecursionError in Python)
Python detects it and optimizes it into a loop
why: Each call adds a stack frame. Without a stopping point, frames pile up until the recursion limit is hit.
4 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 10: each call adds its n to the result of the smaller call.
The print happens *after* the recursive call returns, so the deepest call (n=1) prints first.

q: Time complexity of naive recursive Fibonacci?
why: Each call branches into two, so the tree has about 2ⁿ nodes (the same subproblems are recomputed).

q: Space complexity of naive recursive fib(n)?
why: Only one root-to-leaf path is on the call stack at a time, and the deepest path has n calls.
Two calls per level and log n levels → 2^(log n) = n calls. Compute half once and square it for O(log n).

q: A recursive solution recomputes the same sub-problems many times. What's the standard fix?
options: Use a while loop with the same logic
why: Caching turns repeated work into lookups. This is top-down dynamic programming.
